A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAM research work. All 22 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRAM retrieval and classification experiments in Section 4, plus loss ablations, modality-gap measurements and additional retrieval results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original GRAM experiments and outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix B. These qualify as original empirical results even though they are unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same Gramian volume measure, normalized embeddings, contrastive and data-anchor matching losses, and model architecture. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use VAST27M pretraining and the same downstream datasets: MSR-VTT, DiDeMo, ActivityNet, VATEX, AudioCaps and VGGSound. Task coverage, modality combinations and the depth-modality extension are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments in Tables 1–3 and 8–11, including VAST, LanguageBind and the other listed baselines. Table 6 also retains the same loss-function comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1/Table 5 retain identical splits, sample sizes, frame counts, training budgets, batch sizes and model configurations. Evaluation metrics and zero-shot versus fine-tuning procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The correlation analysis, latent-space visualization, modality-scaling experiment, loss ablations, training curves, modality-gap analysis and qualitative retrieval examples are all retained unchanged in Sections 3.5 and 4 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the correlation analysis in Section 3.5. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains GRAM T-VAS MSR-VTT R@1 values of 64.0 for T2V and 64.8 for V2T, while Figure 3 retains Pearson correlation 0.923.

T1.justification: The Gram-matrix definition, volume theorem and mathematical reasoning are identical. Appendix A retains the same volume proof, three-modality determinant expansion and two-modality angular derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about joint multimodal alignment, scaling from 2 to n modalities, GRAM as a performance metric and improved downstream performance. The abstract's grammar correction does not alter claim scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including weak audio-video correspondence in some datasets in Section 4.2, non-informative volume when k exceeds n in Section 3.2, and the unproven relationship between modality gap and performance in Appendix B.3.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimizer, hyperparameters, dataset-processing information and model details remain identical. The project link and code/pretrained-model availability statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Wang et al. (2019) VATEX reference only receives venue-wording and capitalization edits; it remains the same cited work.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Under review' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', and the arXiv version/date updates. The abstract corrects '2 to n modality' to '2 to n modalities', and the VATEX reference is standardized. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–11 retain identical graphics, captions, formatting and placement. Page organization is unchanged; the header and localized text edits do not introduce a layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 makes only publication-metadata updates and very small grammatical and bibliographic edits. The methods, proofs, empirical evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including both appendices, so these edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
